newsitem.title: CANADA: BHP hopes for diamond mine approval soon.
newsitem.headline: BHP hopes for diamond mine approval soon.

text.p: Australia's Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd said Monday that it hopes a delay in receiving final Canadian government approval for its Arctic diamond mine lasts no more than a day or two.
Earlier a government spokeswoman in Ottawa said Monday target 7 for final approval of the Lac de Gras diamond mine in the Northwest Territories would not be met.
"We're hoping it's just a one or two day delay. If not, it could be a problem," said a BHP spokeswoman. BHP has 51 percent of the project in a joint venture with Dia Met Minerals Ltd.
When it announced approval in principle for the project in August, the government said it would seek to grant final approval in 60 days.

The BHP spokeswoman said the company needs assurance that it can proceed with the project. Every day is critical because of a short winter season in which construction materials can be trucked to the site. BHP must order specialty steel and other goods to coincide with that season. The spokeswoman said the company had spent C$200 million to date on the project and forecast spending of C$20 million more a month. The mine is estimated to cost C$860 million in total when it is completed.
